summary: check:utilities read `border-b` as a colour named `b` and demanded --color-b. Every border in the library until now was either a full box (`border`) or a coloured side (`border-b-elevated`), so nothing had ever written the bare directional WIDTH — Table's row divider is the first, and the gate rejected a correct utility. The border namespace now skips a bare side keyword (x/y/t/r/b/l/s/e) while still resolving the colour in `border-b-elevated` and `border-elevated`. Probed both ways before and after: a typo in either the sided or the unsided colour form is still caught, and bare widths pass.

migration.manual: Tooling only — no distributed file changes. Nothing to do downstream.
